narration.text: A freelancer's receivables, collected. This is a chore for a solo product designer in Brooklyn, trading as a one-person LLC, with seven clients: three force a supplier portal (Coupa, Ariba, Tipalti), the rest pay by email invoice. The invoice leaves QuickBooks, and then it disappears. Athena works it across 6 portals: QuickBooks, Chase Business, Coupa Supplier Portal, SAP Business Network, Tipalti supplier hub and Gmail. On the bench, she found 4 of 5 eligible items, worth 21,100 dollars of the 21,550 dollars there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 9 traps, and she walked past 9. Among them: Acme's Ariba shows payment scheduled on Net 120; the contract says 30 days and governs. Orbit kept 500 dollars, and the contract's late-delivery credit lets it. She took 4 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 4 hours, so she was about 69 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 30 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
